figure_candidates.label: Figure 1
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 1. Cyclooligomer depsipeptide (COD) synthetases and dissection of BbBEAS to splitting unit pairs (SUPs). A. Domain organization and
structures of the products of COD synthetases BbBEAS (beauvericin), ESYN (enniatin B), BbBSLS (bassianolide) and PFSYN (PF1022A). A:
adenylation domain; T: thiolation domain; C: condensation domain; M: N-methyltransferase domain; CT: terminal condensation domain. B.
Domain organization of BbBEAS and the proposed assembly of beauvericin. Both T2a and T2b contribute to the biosynthesis of beauvericin, with T2a
playing a dominant role.[13] C. Production of BbBEAS SUPs in S. cerevisiae BJ5464-NpgA and the relative yield of beauvericin as compared to that of
the wild type enzyme. The grafted docking domain pair PaxB CDD/PaxC NDD,[24] and the synthetic zipper pair SZ 17/18[25] are shown by grey
connector symbols. Data are the meanSD calculated from three independent transformants.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 2
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 2. Optimization of the duplicate T1 splitting strategy with BbBEAS. A. Sequence alignment of the linker region between A1sub-T1 in BbBEAS
with the corresponding linkers in selected fungal NRPSs (BbBSLS, ESYN, and PFSYN synthesize cyclooligomer depsipeptides, DtxS1 produces
destruxins, PsVdoB yields the cyclodipeptide cyclopeptin, and FMQA affords the tripeptide indole alkaloid fumiquinazoline F), and a characterized
bacterial NRPS (LgrA, the gramicidin synthase subunit A). Amino acids conserved in >70% of the selected proteins are in red, >50% are marked
with blue boxes. The conserved motif PxxxxGKxDRxxL(I/V) is marked with a black box. Amino acid numbering is for BbBEAS. The evaluated start
sites for the downstream splitting units are indicated with green circles; the optimal site is emphasized with a red star. Structure elements: spiral,
α-helix; arrow, β-sheet. B. Left, structural alignment of the AlphaFold2 model for the A1-L2-T1 domains of BbBEAS (in blue) with LgrA in the
thiolation state (in light yellow; 6MG0[15c]). Black dashed circle, the extended helix α5 in BbBEAS (R1009-K1022). Right, the overall structure of A1sub-
T1 as a cartoon. Secondary structures are numbered sequentially, and the evaluated start sites for the downstream subunit are indicated. The
optimal site is shown in red. C. BEA (1) yields of BbBEAS SUPs with duplicated T1 domains and different split sites. Percentages are the meanSD
calculated from three biologically independent replicates, relative to the BEA yield of the wild type enzyme.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 3
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 3. Combinatorial biosynthesis of fungal cyclodepsipeptides. A. Reciprocal subunit exchanges vs. module replacements in chimeric proteins
with BbBEAS, BbBSLS, and ESYN.[13b,19b] B. Dissected subunits vs. chimeric enzymes for PFSYN-BbBEAS and PsVdoB-BbBEAS hybrids. Chimeric
enzymes or SUP combinations were produced in S. cerevisiae BJ5464-NpgA, except for the PsVdoB-BbBEAS hybrids whose encoding genes were
transformed into A. nidulans ~ST~EM[34] (highlighted with a star). Split sites or switchover sites are indicated for the subunit exchanges or the
chimeric enzymes, respectively. At least three independent transformants were used for the quantification. The meanSD are shown. ND: Not
detected.

figure_candidates.label: Figure 4
figure_candidates.caption:
Figure 4. Reprogramming the biosynthesis of cyclodepsipeptides with fungal NRPSs. The A1 domain of BbBEAS was replaced with A domains from
DtxS1, PsVdoB, or PFSYN, respectively, to generate unnatural SUPs and chimeric single-subunit control enzymes. The resulting hybrid enzymes
were produced in S. cerevisiae BJ5464-NpgA (DtxS1 or PFSYN exchanges) or A. nidulans ~ST~EM[34] (PsVdoB as the donor). At least three
independent transformants were used to calculate the meanSD shown.
